predecessors.name: Khedivate of Egypt
predecessors.text: the Egyptian Sudan, taken piecemeal by the Ansar between 1882 and 1885: Kordofan, Darfur, Khartoum, Kassala, Sennar

successors.name: Anglo-Egyptian Sudan
successors.text: the Sudan, reconquered 1896-1898 and ruled 'in theory as a condominium with Egypt but in practice as a colony'

ledger.x: 1881: Muhammad Ahmad proclaims himself the Mahdi at the start of the Mahdist War against Egyptian rule.
1882: the Ansar take Al Ubayyid and Kordofan.
1883: Darfur falls to the Mahdists.
July 1884: the Mahdists take the Kingdom of Taqali.
1885: Kassala and Sennar fall.
1885: the Mahdists destroy Ottoman Khartoum and build a new capital at Omdurman.
1885: the Ansar begin to move into the southern region.
1885: the rest of the Egyptian Sudan falls to the Ansar.
26 January 1885: the Ansar take Khartoum.
January 1886: a Mahdist army invades Ethiopia.
1889: the Ethiopian front closes after Gallabat.
1889: Equatoria passes to the Mahdists.
1894: the Italians take Kassala.
1895: Cliopatria's shape loses 25,000 km2 in the south (22.9E-32.1E, 2.0N-10.9N).
7 June 1896: the Dongola Expedition fights its first serious engagement.
September 1896: Kitchener takes Dongola.
7 August 1897: Abu Hamed falls.
1898: the Mahdist hold on the Nuba Mountains ends with the restoration of the Makk.
2 September 1898: the Anglo-Egyptian army takes Omdurman.
September 1898: Darfur leaves the Mahdist State.
September 1898: the Nile-valley campaign ends with Omdurman; the Khalifa escapes to Kordofan and the Mahdist remnant lasts to November 1899.
November 1899: the remnant is lost.
24-25 November 1899: the Khalifa dies at Umm Diwaykarat and the Mahdist State ends.

wars.name: Mahdist War
wars.outcome: Anglo-Egyptian victory: Omdurman falls on 2 September 1898, the Khalifa is killed at Umm Diwaykarat in November 1899 and Sudan becomes the Anglo-Egyptian condominium (Sudan Convention of 18 January 1899).

certainty.note: No treaty or survey line fixes the Mahdist frontiers: Egypt at Wadi Halfa, Ethiopia near Gallabat, Italian Eritrea at Kassala, the Congo in Equatoria.
